# CS 29.923 — Rotor drive system and control mechanism tests

> [!summary]
> CS 29.923 is the endurance test of the rotor drive system and rotor control
> mechanism of a large rotorcraft. It is a CS-29 specification, not a CS-E one,
> and the rotorcraft applicant owns it. The test runs for at least 200 hours in
> ten-hour cycles, plus the time the OEI runs need. Each cycle steps through
> take-off, maximum continuous, 90%, 80% and 60% torque. Overspeed, engine
> malfunction, clutch, control position and lubricant conditions are added.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-29's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Test each rotor drive system and rotor control mechanism, as prescribed in (b) to (n) and (p), for at least 200 hours plus the time required to meet the requirements of (b)(2), (b)(3) and (k). | Required |
| **(a)(1)** | Use ten-hour test cycles, except that the test cycle must be extended to include the OEI test of (b)(2) and (k) where OEI ratings are requested. | Required |
| **(a)(2)** | Conduct the tests on the rotorcraft. | Required |
| **(a)(3)(i)** | Determine the test torque and rotational speed by the powerplant limitations. | Required |
| **(a)(3)(ii)** | Absorb the test torque by the rotors to be approved for the rotorcraft. | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | Make the take-off torque run 1 hour of alternate runs of 5 minutes at take-off torque and the maximum speed for use with take-off torque, and 5 minutes at as low an engine idle speed as practicable, except as prescribed in (b)(2) and (b)(3). | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | Declutch the engine from the rotor drive system and, where a rotor brake is furnished and so intended, apply it during the first minute of the idle run. During the remaining 4 minutes of the idle run, engage the clutch so that the engine drives the rotors at the minimum practical rpm. | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | Accelerate the engine and the rotor drive system at the maximum rate. When declutching the engine, decelerate it rapidly enough to allow the operation of the overrunning clutch. | Required |
| **(b)(2)** | For helicopters for which the use of a 2½-minute OEI rating is requested, conduct the take-off run as prescribed in (b)(1), except for the third and sixth runs. | Required if claimed |
| **(b)(2)(i)** | Each of those runs must consist of at least one period of 2½ minutes with take-off torque and the maximum speed for use with take-off torque on all engines. | Required if claimed |
| **(b)(2)(ii)** | Each of those runs must consist of at least one period, for each engine in sequence, during which that engine simulates a power failure and the remaining engines are run at the 2½-minute OEI torque and the maximum speed for use with 2½-minute OEI torque for 2½ minutes. | Required if claimed |
| **(b)(3)** | For multi-engine, turbine-powered rotorcraft for which the use of 30-second/2-minute OEI power is requested, conduct the take-off run as prescribed in (b)(1) except as set out in (b)(3)(i) to (b)(3)(iii). | Required if claimed |
| **(b)(3)(i)** | Immediately following any one 5-minute power-on run required by (b)(1), simulate a failure for each power source in turn, and apply the maximum torque and the maximum speed for use with the 30-second OEI power to the remaining affected drive system power inputs for not less than 30 seconds. | Required if claimed |
| **(b)(3)(i)** | Follow each application of 30-second OEI power by two applications of the maximum torque and the maximum speed for use with the 2 minute OEI power for not less than 2 minutes each. The second application must follow a period at stabilised continuous or 30-minute OEI power, whichever the applicant requests. | Required if claimed |
| **(b)(3)(i)** | Conduct at least one run sequence from a simulated flight idle condition. Where the run is conducted on a bench test, conduct the test sequence following stabilisation at take-off power. | Required if claimed |
| **(b)(3)(ii)** | An affected power input includes all parts of the rotor drive system which can be adversely affected by the application of higher or asymmetric torque and speed prescribed by the test. | Statement |
| **(b)(3)(iii)** | This test may be conducted on a representative bench test facility when engine limitations either preclude repeated use of this power or would result in premature engine removals during the test. | Permitted |
| **(b)(3)(iii)** | Make the loads, the vibration frequency and the methods of application to the affected rotor drive system components representative of rotorcraft conditions. The test components must be those used to show compliance with the remainder of the paragraph. | Required |
| **(c)** | Conduct three hours of continuous operation at maximum continuous torque and the maximum speed for use with maximum continuous torque, as set out in (c)(1) to (c)(3). | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Operate the main rotor controls at a minimum of 15 times each hour through the main rotor pitch positions of maximum vertical thrust, maximum forward thrust component, maximum aft thrust component, maximum left thrust component, and maximum right thrust component. | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | The control movements need not produce loads or blade flapping motion exceeding the maximum loads of motions encountered in flight. | Relief |
| **(c)(2)** | Operate the directional controls at a minimum of 15 times each hour through the control extremes of maximum right turning torque, neutral torque as required by the power applied to the main rotor, and maximum left turning torque. | Required |
| **(c)(3)** | Hold each maximum control position for at least 10 seconds, and make the rate of change of control position at least as rapid as that for normal operation. | Required |
| **(d)** | Conduct one hour of continuous operation at 90% of maximum continuous torque and the maximum speed for use with 90% of maximum continuous torque. | Required |
| **(e)** | Conduct one hour of continuous operation at 80% of maximum continuous torque and the minimum speed for use with 80% of maximum continuous torque. | Required |
| **(f)** | Conduct two hours of continuous operation at 60% of maximum continuous torque and the minimum speed for use with 60% of maximum continuous torque. Where the use of either 30-minute OEI power or continuous OEI power is requested, this run is 1 hour. | Required |
| **(g)** | Determine whether malfunctioning of components, such as the engine fuel or ignition systems, or whether unequal engine power can cause dynamic conditions detrimental to the drive system. | Required |
| **(g)** | If so, accomplish a suitable number of hours of operation under those conditions, 1 hour of which must be included in each cycle, and the remaining hours of which must be accomplished at the end of the 20 cycles. | Required |
| **(g)** | If no detrimental condition results, conduct an additional hour of operation in compliance with (b), in accordance with the run schedule of (b)(1) and without consideration of (b)(2). | Required |
| **(h)** | Conduct one hour of continuous operation at maximum continuous torque and the maximum power-on overspeed expected in service, assuming that speed and torque limiting devices, if any, function properly. | Required |
| **(i)** | When the rotor controls are not being cycled during the endurance tests, operate the rotor, using the procedures prescribed in (c), to produce each of the maximum thrust positions for the percentages of test time in (i)(1) to (i)(5). | Required |
| **(i)** | The control positions need not produce loads or blade flapping motion exceeding the maximum loads or motions encountered in flight. | Relief |
| **(i)(1)** | Full vertical thrust, 20%. | Required |
| **(i)(2)** | Forward thrust component, 50%. | Required |
| **(i)(3)** | Right thrust component, 10%. | Required |
| **(i)(4)** | Left thrust component, 10%. | Required |
| **(i)(5)** | Aft thrust component, 10%. | Required |
| **(j)** | Make a total of at least 400 clutch and brake engagements, including the engagements of (b), during the take-off torque runs and, if necessary, at each change of torque and speed throughout the test. | Required |
| **(j)** | In each clutch engagement, accelerate the shaft on the driven side of the clutch from rest. Accomplish the clutch engagements at the speed and by the method prescribed by the applicant. | Required |
| **(j)** | During deceleration after each clutch engagement, stop the engines rapidly enough to allow the engines to be automatically disengaged from the rotors and rotor drives. | Required |
| **(j)** | Where a rotor brake is installed for stopping the rotor, disengage the clutch during brake engagements above 40% of maximum continuous rotor speed, allow the rotors to decelerate to 40% of maximum continuous rotor speed, and then apply the rotor brake. | Required |
| **(j)** | Where the clutch design does not allow stopping the rotors with the engine running, or where no clutch is provided, stop the engine before each application of the rotor brake and start it immediately after the rotors stop. | Required |
| **(k)(1)** | For rotorcraft for which the use of 30-minute OEI power is requested, conduct a run at 30-minute OEI torque and the maximum speed for use with 30-minute OEI torque. For each engine, in sequence, that engine must be inoperative and the remaining engines must be run for a 30-minute period. | Required if claimed |
| **(k)(2)** | For rotorcraft for which the use of continuous OEI power is requested, conduct a run at continuous OEI torque and the maximum speed for use with continuous OEI torque. For each engine, in sequence, that engine must be inoperative and the remaining engines must be run for 1 hour. | Required if claimed |
| **(k)(3)** | The number of periods prescribed in (k)(1) or (k)(2) may not be less than the number of engines, nor less than two. | Required |
| **(l)** | Reserved. CS-29 states no requirement at this sub-point. | Statement |
| **(m)** | Investigate any components that are affected by manoeuvring and gust loads for the same flight conditions as are the main rotors, and determine their service lives by fatigue tests or by other acceptable methods. | Required |
| **(m)** | Provide a level of safety equal to that of the main rotors for the components in (m)(1) to (m)(3). | Required |
| **(m)(1)** | Each component in the rotor drive system whose failure would cause an uncontrolled landing. | Required |
| **(m)(2)** | Each component essential to the phasing of rotors on multi-rotor rotorcraft, or that furnishes a driving link for the essential control of rotors in autorotation. | Required |
| **(m)(3)** | Each component common to two or more engines on multi-engine rotorcraft. | Required |
| **(n)** | Subject each rotor drive system designed to operate at two or more gear ratios to special testing for durations necessary to substantiate the safety of the rotor drive system. | Required |
| **(o)** | Each part tested must be in a serviceable condition at the end of the tests. Conduct no intervening disassembly which might affect test results. | Required |
| **(p)** | To be approved for use in rotor drive and control systems, lubricants must meet the specifications of lubricants used during the tests prescribed by this paragraph. | Required |
| **(p)** | Additional or alternate lubricants may be qualified by equivalent testing or by comparative analysis of lubricant specifications and rotor drive and control system characteristics. | Permitted |
| **(p)(1)** | Conduct at least three 10-hour cycles required by this paragraph with transmission and gearbox lubricant temperatures, at the location prescribed for measurement, not lower than the maximum operating temperature for which approval is requested. | Required |
| **(p)(2)** | For pressure lubricated systems, conduct at least three 10-hour cycles required by this paragraph with the lubricant pressure, at the location prescribed for measurement, not higher than the minimum operating pressure for which approval is requested. | Required |
| **(p)(3)** | Apply the test conditions of (p)(1) and (p)(2) simultaneously, and extend them to include operation at any one-engine-inoperative rating for which approval is requested. | Required |

Four blocks of the schedule are conditional on a rating. Sub-points (b)(2),
(b)(3), (k)(1) and (k)(2) each open "For rotorcraft for which the use of" a
named OEI power "is requested" [ext CS 29.923(k)(2)]. Nothing obliges an
applicant to request the rating; once it is requested, the runs are mandatory.
That is the Required if claimed strength, and `## Bearing on this engine`
settles which of the four arise for this engine.

The test length is stated twice over. Sub-point (a) asks for "at least 200
hours plus the time required to meet the requirements of sub-paragraphs (b)(2),
(b)(3) and (k)" [ext CS 29.923(a)], and sub-point (a)(1) asks for ten-hour test
cycles [ext CS 29.923(a)(1)]. Sub-point (g) then refers to "the end of the 20
cycles" [ext CS 29.923(g)]. Twenty cycles of ten hours are the 200 hours, and
the OEI runs extend the cycle rather than replace part of it
[ext CS 29.923(a)(1)].

Sub-point (l) is marked "Reserved." in CS-29 Amendment 12
[ext CS 29.923(l)]. The row records that the sub-point was read and carries no
obligation, so that its absence is not read as an omission.

Sub-point (k)(3) sets a floor on the OEI runs rather than a count: the number of
periods "may not be less than the number of engines, nor may it be less than
two" [ext CS 29.923(k)(3)]. The row is Required, because the constraint is
mandatory.

The counterpart paragraph, [[CS 27.923]], carries a different schedule, a
different OEI regime and a shorter list of runs. The comparison between the two
codes is recorded there. The additional tests of the same rotor drive system
are a separate paragraph, [[CS 29.927]].

## Bearing on this engine

CS 29.923 creates no CS-E obligation. The test is run on the rotor drive system
and the rotor control mechanism, which are not part of the engine type design.
One sub-point nevertheless makes the whole schedule depend on engine data:
sub-point (a)(3)(i) fixes the test torque and rotational speed as
"Determined by the powerplant limitations" [ext CS 29.923(a)(3)(i)]. Every
torque and every speed named in (b) to (p) follows from that sentence. The
limitations are declared under [[CS-E 40]] and reach the installer through the
installation instructions of [[CS-E 20]].

The two all-engines-operating blocks rest on ratings this engine declares.
Take-off torque and the maximum speed for use with it [ext CS 29.923(b)(1)]
rest on Take-off Power [CS-E 40(a)]. Maximum continuous torque, and the 90%,
80% and 60% steps derived from it [ext CS 29.923(d)], [ext CS 29.923(e)],
[ext CS 29.923(f)], rest on Maximum Continuous Power [CS-E 40(a)]. Both ratings
are mandatory for every engine, and the applicant declares both.

The four conditional blocks divide as follows, against the ratings declared in
`engine_profile.md`.

- **2½-minute OEI rating**, sub-point (b)(2). **Not declared.** 2½-Minute OEI
  Power [CS-E 40(b)(3)(iii)] is listed as not claimed, so the third and sixth
  runs of the take-off run stay as sub-point (b)(1) writes them.
- **30-second/2-minute OEI power**, sub-point (b)(3). **Both declared**, as
  30-Second OEI Power [CS-E 40(b)(3)(i)] and 2-Minute OEI Power
  [CS-E 40(b)(3)(ii)]. The sequence of (b)(3)(i) arises.
- **30-minute OEI power**, sub-point (k)(1). **Not declared.** 30-Minute OEI
  Power [CS-E 40(b)(3)(iv)] is listed as not claimed, so the 30-minute
  single-engine periods do not arise.
- **Continuous OEI power**, sub-point (k)(2). **Declared**, as Continuous OEI
  Power [CS-E 40(b)(3)(v)]. The 1-hour single-engine periods arise, and
  sub-point (k)(3) sets their number at not less than the number of engines and
  not less than two.

Because continuous OEI power is requested, the reduction in sub-point (f)
applies: the 60% block is 1 hour and not two hours [ext CS 29.923(f)].

The ratings not declared settle one clause that would otherwise be ambiguous.
Sub-point (b)(3)(i) asks that the second 2-minute application follow "a period
at stabilised continuous or 30-minute OEI power" [ext CS 29.923(b)(3)(i)], and
leaves the choice to the applicant. This engine declares Continuous OEI Power
and does not declare 30-Minute OEI Power, so the stabilised period is at
continuous OEI power. Rated 30-Minute Power [CS-E 40(b)(4)] is a different
rating and does not answer the clause; [[CS 27.923]] records why the two must
not be confused.

The lubricant regime reaches the declared OEI ratings as well. Sub-point (p)(3)
asks that the temperature and pressure conditions "must be applied
simultaneously and must be extended to include operation at any
one-engine-inoperative rating for which approval is requested"
[ext CS 29.923(p)(3)]. For this installation that is all three declared OEI
ratings. The lubricant in question is the transmission and gearbox lubricant,
not the engine Oil System of [CS-E 570], and no CS-E obligation follows from it.

Sub-point (h) consumes a second CS-29-only engine data item. The overspeed run
is flown at "the maximum power-on overspeed expected in service, assuming that
speed and torque limiting devices, if any, function properly"
[ext CS 29.923(h)]. [[CS-E 20]] already records one such CS-29-only item, the
rotational speed expected after an engine control device failure, which
[[CS 29.927]] consumes. This is a second, and CS-27 asks for neither: CS 27.923
prescribes no overspeed run [ext CS 27.923].

[VERIFY: whether the maximum power-on overspeed expected in service can be
derived from the engine's declared Maximum Engine Over-speed under [CS-E 830],
or whether it is an installation-derived figure the engine applicant cannot
supply alone. CS 29.923(h) does not say, and `engine_profile.md` lists Maximum
Engine Over-speed among the limits still to be declared.]

Sub-point (g) is written about the engine. It asks the rotorcraft applicant to
determine whether "malfunctioning of components, such as the engine fuel or
ignition systems, or whether unequal engine power can cause dynamic conditions
detrimental to the drive system" [ext CS 29.923(g)]. The failure modes of the
engine fuel and ignition systems are engine-side, and they are assessed in the
safety analysis of [[CS-E 510]]; for a full-authority EECS the control side is
assessed under [[CS-E 50]]. The installer cannot run this determination without
knowing which engine malfunctions are credible and what power asymmetry they
produce, so the data belongs in the installation instructions of [[CS-E 20]].

Sub-point (b)(1) consumes engine idle and acceleration data. It asks for 5
minutes at "as low an engine idle speed as practicable", for the engine to
drive the rotors at the minimum practical rpm, and for the engine and rotor
drive system to be accelerated at the maximum rate [ext CS 29.923(b)(1)].
Sub-point (b)(3)(i) adds a run sequence from a simulated flight idle condition.
The idle condition the engine can offer, and the rate at which it accelerates
away from it, are engine data proved under [[CS-E 745]].

The engine's own endurance test is [[CS-E 740]]. It is run on the engine and it
proves the engine. CS 29.923 is run on the rotorcraft and it proves the rotor
drive system. Neither schedule substitutes for the other, and the bench test
relief in (b)(3)(iii) exists because the engine may not be able to sustain the
transmission's programme: it is available only "when engine limitations either
preclude repeated use of this power or would result in premature engine
removals during the test" [ext CS 29.923(b)(3)(iii)]. Whether it is available
depends on the usage limits the engine applicant declares for the 30-Second and
2-Minute OEI Power ratings.

Which of the two codes applies is still open. [[CS-E 30]] carries that item, and
the schedules differ enough that the answer changes the run programme entirely.
